title: Trailer shot plates are all asked for the same generic emblem
body:
## Summary
render-plates renders every picture unit, shot units included, and a shot unit's subject falls through `subjectFor(frameOfUnit(u))`, which has no entry for a trailer kind and returns the explainer's 'statement' shape, so every trailer shot is billed for 'One large simple emblem centred alone in the frame'.

## Description
lib/producers/frames.ts:227-229 `plateRequest`: `u.plate.subject?.trim() || subjectFor(frameOfUnit(u))`. frameOfUnit casts a shot unit's `beatKind` (`reset`, `peak`, ...) to `BeatKind` (lib/frames/picture/unit.ts:252-259, whose own comment says shot units never reach it); lib/frames/frames.ts `subjectFor` looks `PROBLEM_OF[kind]` up, gets undefined, and returns `shape.statement`. packages/producers/src/frames/define.ts:54-58 `render-plates` selects `v.units.filter(needsPlate)` with no `kind` filter, so trailer shot units (lib/frames/picture/unit.ts trailerUnits) are rendered. The shot lane already composes the right subject - lib/frames/shotPrompt.ts `actionFor(shot)` from the role x size recipe and staging (`unit.staging`) - and nothing on the render path calls it. The fixture port has the mirror defect: app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/fixtureFrames.ts:93 falls back to `u.line`, the beat's sentence, which shotPrompt.ts says must never reach a model. Fixed: a shot unit's plate subject is `actionFor` over its staging (or the plate's stored subject), on both sides.

## Flow
- a trailer project with a composed spine -> units are shot units (trailerUnits)
- render-plates (DRY) books one plate per shot unit
- observe: every booked subject is the identical statement-shape sentence; the role x size recipes (setup:EWS, peak:ECU, ...) appear in none

## Expected impact
A trailer's plates differ per shot as the shot lane designed, and the operator stops paying for N copies of one generic emblem. Could break: a stored plate subject keeps priority, so only unsubjected shots change.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality/spend - each trailer shot plate is asked for its own staged subject
Before: distinct plate subjects across a trailer chain's shot units (the probe TEASER: 6 beats -> 12 shots): 1, the 'statement' shape; 0 of 12 carry their shotPrompt recipe
After: one subject per shot from actionFor(staging) (9 role x size recipes reachable); 0 fall back to 'statement'
Method: simulation - walked plateRequest -> frameOfUnit -> subjectFor on a shot unit (PROBLEM_OF has no trailer kind); out of this round's paths (lib/producers, packages/producers, app port), so no DRY job was driven
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a DRY render-plates job in tests/next-server/producer-step-frames.test.ts over a trailer spine: count distinct booked subjects and assert none equals subjectFor's statement shape

title: One malformed v1 frames row aborts the whole archive import
body:
## Summary
`framesV1ToV2` throws on a v1 frames object it cannot read, and the importer calls it with no catch, so a single bad `frames` row throws out of stageStep -> stageProject -> the archive staging instead of being graded `data-only` with the door's sentence.

## Description
lib/frames/picture/migrate.ts framesIn throws `frames is not a list` / `frames[i] is not a frame` (its header used to promise 'the registry turns [it] into a malformed refusal'; that registry retired with app/_phases). lib/import/steps.ts:62 `lift` calls `framesV1ToV2({ ...data })` bare; stageStep (:82) and lib/import/project.ts:135/214 map over rows with no try. lib/import/steps.ts's own header: 'NOTHING IS DROPPED SILENTLY ... a record its door refuses, with the door's sentence'. Fixed: lift catches the walk's throw and returns its message as the refusal string (data-only), as it already does for a too-new version.

## Flow
- build an archive whose v1 frames row is `{ frames: "x", renderId: "r" }`
- stage the import
- observe: Error 'frames is not a list' escapes; no project is staged (expected: that row data-only, the rest full)

## Expected impact
A partly damaged v1 export imports everything it can and names the one row it could not. Could break: nothing that passes today.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a bad v1 frames row is one graded loss, not a failed import
Before: probe: framesV1ToV2({frames:'x'}) THROWS Error 'frames is not a list' (run this round); 0 catch sites between it and the archive staging
After: the row comes back loss.grade 'data-only', reason 'frames is not a list'; other rows staged
Method: probe - the throw reproduced on the real module; the fix site is lib/import/steps.ts, another context's path
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a stageStep case (tests/next-server import tests) with a malformed v1 frames row: throws on base, loss data-only after; seed by removing the catch

title: parseFramesRecord is v1's door, kept alive by one probe
body:
## Summary
`parseFramesRecord` (lib/frames/picture/migrate.ts) is the v1 app's v2 door; its only consumer is tests/golden-path/picture-unit.probe.spec.ts, and it is the only reason migrate.ts imports lib/steps/recordRegistry.

## Description
The live v2 door is @gt/domain FRAMES (packages/domain/src/steps/frames.ts, v3), reached from lib/import/steps.ts through encodeRecord. parseFramesRecord validates a different, weaker shape (no beatRef check - a unit with no beatRef makes framesFromUnits throw a TypeError instead of refusing) and pins v1 behaviour the product no longer runs. Fixed: picture-unit's walk case asserts through the importer's path (framesV1ToV2 -> encodeRecord('frames', ...)), parseFramesRecord and its recordRegistry import go.

## Flow
- grep parseFramesRecord: 1 test consumer, 0 product
- move the probe case onto encodeRecord
- delete parseFramesRecord

## Expected impact
One door for the frames record instead of two that disagree. Could break: the probe's assertion on the rebuilt `frames` shadow (v3 has none) must be restated.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one validator per persisted shape
Before: consumers of parseFramesRecord: 1 (a probe), product 0; doors for the frames record: 2
After: 0 consumers, 1 door; migrate.ts -> lib/steps/recordRegistry edge 1 -> 0
Method: probe - zero-consumer grep run this round; the probe rewrite (tests/golden-path, M with semantic change) is not landed unread
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: picture-unit.probe walk case rewritten over encodeRecord('frames', lift(...)); red when framesV1ToV2 drops a shot unit

title: FrameClip does not declare the blob and model the motion producer writes
body:
## Summary
lib/producers/motion.ts writes `clip: { ...x.clip, status: "rendered", blob, model }` onto a picture unit through a `written<>` cast, and `FrameClip` (lib/frames/frames.ts) declares neither field, so no reader can type them.

## Description
FrameClip has status/motion/note only. motion.ts:216 lands blob and model; lib/library/feeds/kernel.ts:13 reads `clip.blob` generically; tests/next-server/producer-step-motion.test.ts:115 indexes `clip["blob"]`. Fixed: FrameClip gains optional `blob?: BlobRef; model?: string`, and motion.ts drops the cast.

## Flow
- grep clip.blob writers/readers
- add the optional fields
- remove the cast at motion.ts:216; typecheck

## Expected impact
A rendered clip's bytes are a typed field. Could break: nothing at runtime (type-only).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - persisted fields declared on their type
Before: persisted clip fields with no declaration: 2 (blob, model); `written<>` casts on the write: 1
After: 0 undeclared; 0 casts
Method: simulation - read the write site and the type; the cast removal is in lib/producers (another context)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
lib/producers/motion.ts:216 return ... { ...x, clip: { ...x.clip, status: "rendered", blob: m["blob"], model: m["model"] } };
lib/frames/frames.ts FrameClip { status; motion; note? }
instrument: typecheck with the cast at lib/producers/motion.ts:216 removed: red before the FrameClip fields, green after

title: The fixture port re-implements isStalePlate
body:
## Summary
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/fixtureFrames.ts:96 `owes` restates frames.ts `isStalePlate`'s rule inline (ready + renderedSubject vs subject, trimmed) instead of calling it.

## Description
isStalePlate (lib/frames/frames.ts) is the one rule for 'a plate behind its subject' and has 4 consumers; fixtureFrames.ts:96 writes a second copy (`u.plate.renderedSubject !== undefined && u.plate.subject !== undefined && u.plate.subject.trim() !== u.plate.renderedSubject.trim()`). Today they agree; the next change to one (e.g. whitespace normalisation) splits the fixture's 'owes' from the real side. Fixed: owes calls isStalePlate(frameOfUnit(u)).

## Flow
- diff the two predicates
- replace the inline copy
- a fixture-port case: a stale ready plate owes a render

## Expected impact
One staleness rule on both sides of the port. Could break: nothing (same truth table).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one implementation of one rule
Before: implementations of the plate-staleness rule: 2
After: 1
Method: simulation - read both sites; the site is the app port (another context)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
lib/frames/frames.ts isStalePlate
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/fixtureFrames.ts:96 export const owes = (u) => u.plate.state !== "ready" || (u.plate.renderedSubject !== undefined && ...)

title: The scene contract carries no motif threads and no boundary class
body:
## Summary
SCENE_SCHEMA and SceneSpec (lib/frames/sceneSpec.ts) have no field for a named motif thread or for the join between adjacent frames, which the frame-direction golden path's techniques motif-establish-vary-payoff and boundary-transition-class make part of direction.

## Description
ai-registry media-generation/visual-generation/frame-direction: 'Motifs are managed as named threads with explicit lifecycle operations, so a change or a reprise provably refers to something the viewer has already seen', and every boundary is declared carry / agent / refresh. SceneSpec holds beatAt, subject, motion, rationale, elements, texts only; the direction pass can therefore not be checked for a reprise of a motif never established, nor for a hold beat that silently refreshes. Fixed would be a new authored field pair plus parseScene checks - a capability the context's declared scope (validate the engine's output into frames, per-beat proposal) does not name, so it is a direction for the operator.

## Flow
- read frame-direction.md + the two techniques
- diff against SCENE_SCHEMA
- decide whether Frames authors threads/boundaries

## Expected impact
The direction pass can be held to the arc, not just the frame. Could break: every stored proposal shape and the engine prompt.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - direction checked against the cut's arc
Before: techniques of the governing subject with no field in the contract: 2 of 7
After: 0 of 7 (if adopted)
Method: simulation - read the golden path and the schema; no figure without building the capability
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
lib/frames/sceneSpec.ts SCENE_SCHEMA properties: beatAt, subject, motion, rationale, elements, texts
ai-registry knowledge/media-generation/visual-generation/frame-direction/techniques/{motif-establish-vary-payoff,boundary-transition-class}.md
